name: Bogra Sweet Curd (বগুড়ার দই)
desc: Boiled rich creamy cow milk reduced for hours in red earthen pots with caramelized brown sugar, producing velvety thick curd with an unmatched smoky aroma.
origin: Sherpur, Bogura (Started by Gouro Gopal Ghosh in 1930s)

name: Natore Kachagolla (নাটোরের কাঁচাগোল্লা)
desc: Soft, melt-in-mouth reduced pure milk chhana kneaded with mild fragrant sugar syrup and cardamom. Not round, but a heavenly loose chhana delight.
origin: Natore Town (Started by Madhusudan Das in 1760 during Maharani Bhabani rule)

name: Matri Bhandar Rasmalai (মাতৃভাণ্ডার রসমালাই)
desc: Small pillowy cottage cheese balls soaked in slow-condensed thick saffron-flavored clotted cream (malai).
origin: Manoharpur, Cumilla (Invented by brothers Khanindra Sen and Manindra Sen in 1901)

name: Porabari Chamcham (পোড়াবাড়ির চমচম)
desc: Deep golden-brown exterior coated with dry mawa powder, with an ultra-juicy honeyed inner core brewed in sweet Dhaleshwari river water.
origin: Porabari, Tangail (Created by Dasharath Sen in early 19th century)

name: Muktagacha Monda (মুক্তাগাছার মন্ডা)
desc: Flattened disk-shaped sweet of pure chhana and sugar prepared according to a 200-year-old closely guarded family recipe.
origin: Muktagacha, Mymensingh (Created in 1824 by sweetmaker Ram Gopal Modak for Maharaja Suryakanta)

name: Chittagong Mezban Gosht & Chonar Dal (মেজবানি গোশত)
desc: Spicy royal beef feast cooked with indigenous whole spices, mustard oil, white sesame, radhuni and served with yellow split-pea curry.
origin: Centuries-old hospitality tradition of Chattogram community feasts

name: Sylheti Shatkora Beef Curry (সাতকরা দিয়ে গরুর মাংস)
desc: Rich aromatic beef stew simmered with wedges of wild citrus macroptera (Shatkora), infusing a tart, deeply fragrant flavor.
origin: Sylhet foothills and Jaintia tribal cuisine borders

name: Khulna Chui Jhal Mutton & Beef (চুই ঝাল)
desc: Meat cooked with woody stalks of Piper chaba (Chui vine), releasing an earthy horseradish-peppery warmth without burning the stomach.
origin: Chuknagar & Rupsha delta belts of southern Bengal

name: Old Dhaka Bakarkhani (পুরান ঢাকার বাকরখানি)
desc: Crispy, multi-layered flaky flatbread baked in clay tandoor ovens, named after legendary lovers Aga Baker and Khani Begum.
origin: Old Dhaka (Lalbagh, Chawkbazar and Nazira Bazar during 18th century)

name: Nilkantha Seven Layer Tea (সাত রঙের চা)
desc: Seven distinct layers of different density green, lemon, spiced, condensed and black teas served in a single transparent glass without mixing.
origin: Sreemangal, Moulvibazar (Invented by Romesh Ram Gour in 2002)
